t: This is the Hilton London Paddington, once the Great Western Royal Hotel. It forms the main façade of Paddington Station, closing off the end of the train shed. The idea came from Isambard Kingdom Brunel, who was its first managing director. Philip Charles Hardwick designed it, and Prince Albert opened it on 9 June 1854, after 14 months of building. It was meant to rival the great hotels on the Continent. The 2nd Duke of Buckingham and Chandos, a Tory politician and bankrupt, died here in 1861.
